CFML Language Reference: Functions

REFind

Searches a string for the first match of a regular expression and returns its position. Optionally it returns the position and length of the match and of each parenthesized subexpression.

Category

String functions

Syntax

REFind(reg_expression, string [, start ] [, returnsubexpressions ])

Parameters

reg_expression
The regular expression to search for (see below).
string
The string to search.
start
Optional. Position at which to start searching. Default 1.
returnsubexpressions
Optional. Boolean. If true, REFind returns a structure instead of a number. Default false. To use it you must also pass start.

Returns

Without returnsubexpressions: the position of the first match, or 0.

With returnsubexpressions set to true: a structure with two arrays, pos and len. Element 1 of each describes the whole match; elements 2, 3, ... describe the parenthesized subexpressions in order (up to nine). If there is no match, each array holds a single 0.

Usage

The regular expression dialect

KoldFusion implements POSIX extended regular expressions, like ColdFusion 4.5:

Syntax Matches
. any single character
* + ? zero or more, one or more, zero or one of the preceding item
{m} {m,} {m,n} exactly m, at least m, between m and n of the preceding item
[abc] [a-z] [^abc] one character from (or not from) a set or range
^ $ start and end of the string
( ) groups items and marks a subexpression
\. \( \[ ... the special character itself

A vertical bar separates alternatives: cat|dog matches either word.

Inside brackets you can use the POSIX character classes [:alpha:], [:upper:], [:lower:], [:digit:], [:alnum:], [:xdigit:], [:space:], [:punct:], [:print:], [:graph:] and [:cntrl:], for example [[:digit:]]+ or [^[:space:]].

Note  Perl shorthands such as \d, \w and \s are not part of the 4.5 dialect. KoldFusion quietly treats them as [0-9], [A-Za-z0-9_] and [[:space:]], but for portable code use the POSIX classes. Non-greedy quantifiers and look-ahead are not supported.

An invalid expression throws an exception of type Expression. Remember that inside CFOUTPUT a # in a pattern must be written ##.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Text = "Call 555-1234 or 555-9876 before Y2K">
<CFSET Match = REFind("([0-9]{3})-([0-9]{4})", Text, 1, "True")>
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>#Text#</P>
<UL>
<LI>First digit at: #REFind("[[:digit:]]", Text)#
<LI>Second number at: #REFind("[0-9]{3}-", Text, 10)#
<LI>"y2k" (case-sensitive): #REFind("y2k", Text)#
<LI>Whole match: #Mid(Text, Match.pos[1], Match.len[1])#
<LI>Exchange: #Mid(Text, Match.pos[2], Match.len[2])#, line: #Mid(Text, Match.pos[3], Match.len[3])#
</UL>
</CFOUTPUT>
